etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English awakenen or awaknen, from Old English awæcnan or awæcnian, from a- plus wæcnan or wæcnian.

definitions.definition: (transitive, figurative) To bring into action (something previously dormant); to stimulate.

quote.citation: 1951 April, Stirling Everard, “A Matter of Pedigree”, in Railway Magazine, number 600, page 273:
quote.text: On the other hand, the self-cleaning smokebox belongs to the latter-day period of the L.M.S.R., when the visiting U.S.A. 2-8-0s of the war had awakened an interest in such things.

quote.citation: 1984, 20:05 from the start, in Dune‎[1] (Science Fiction), →OCLC:
quote.text: I'll miss the sea. But a person needs new experiences. They draw something deep inside, allowing him to grow. Without change, something sleeps inside us and seldom awakens. The sleeper must awaken.

definitions.definition: (theology) To call to a sense of sin.

quote.text: [This ant] I ſuffered to lye above an hour in the Spirit; and after I had taken it out, and put its body and legs into a natural poſture, remained moveleſs about an hour; but then , upon a ſudden, as if it had been awaken out of a drunken ſleep, it ſuddenly reviv'd and ran away...

definitions.definition: (transitive, figurative) To cause to become aware.
